articles.title: Espí esconde que a Güler no se le puede cambiar
articles.standfirst: La contracrónica del Espanyol- Real Madrid
articles.summary: La contracrónica del Espanyol- Real Madrid
articles.body: El episodio IV del Madrid de Mourinho ya está en marcha. El RCDE Stadium fue el escenario en el que se levantó el telón de la segunda aventura del técnico portugués en la Casa Blanca. El despegue de un proyecto que arranca con la incógnita de si logrará alcanzar el éxito, como ocurrió con el regreso de Carlo Ancelotti en 2021, o si acabará dando la razón al viejo dicho español de que las segundas partes nunca fueron buenas. Ante un Espanyol que repetía en casa después de arrancar LaLiga de manera contundente (3-0 al Levante), el Madrid se encontró con dos partidos. Uno hasta la media hora, en el que fue mucho mejor; otro a partir del momento en el que Vinicius se enfrentó a la grada y encendió una chispa que prendió al equipo de Manolo González para sentirse capaz de todo a base de corazón. Pero no solo se puede mirar a Vinicius. Porque Mbappé tuvo uno de esos partidos en los que parece que la portería es de hockey sobre patines. El francés, Bota de Oro del Mundial, las tuvo de todos los colores. Pero no fue capaz de marcar. El campo del Espanyol sigue en su lista de campos en los que no ha marcado. Y no fue porque su equipo no le encontrara. Todo lo contrario que Carlos Espí. El fichaje de menor rango del Madrid fue el que resolvió el partido. Tres puntos de oro con la firma de un chaval que apunta a dar muchas cosas al Madrid... y a la selección.  Lanzó el portugués un aviso a navegantes en la previa del partido. Una especie de provocación simpática a los periodistas y un avios a quienes viven dentro de la caseta blanca: "El once ya se lo dicho a los jugadores. A ver quién de vosotros tiene mejores contactos". Truco de entrenador curtido, de saber manejar tiempos y espacios. A las 20.11 horas saltó el equipo: Courtois; Dumfries, Konaté, Huijsen, Carreras; Valverde, Bernardo Silva; Güler, Bellingham, Vinicius y Mbappé. Ese quedaba como el primer equipo de Mourinho en LaLiga, con tres de los fichajes y la BMV.  Tardó menos de 10 minutos el Madrid de Mourinho en tomar el mando del partido. De una falta lateral sacada por Vinicius, derribado hasta tres veces en los albores del partido, nació un centro de Güler al corazón del área del Espanyol. Allí apareció Bellingham para aprovechar la pasividad y colapso de la defensa del Espanyol para cabecear a la red. Su nombre aparece en la tabla de los primeros goleadores del Madrid en la Liga. Y, de paso, prolongar el excelente nivel que mostró en el Mundial. Si el 5 anda fuerte y la mezcla con Güler funciona como parece... Tenía el Madrid el partido donde quería. Bellingham campaba a sus anchas. Güler mandaba y mostraba galones de jugador dominante. Entonces no se le ocurrió otra cosa que encararse cerca de su área con un central rival, Riedel. Y después, con la grada. El cloroformo en el que tenía el Madrid al equipo de Manolo González se convirtió en adrenalina perica. Nunca se podrá demostrar si fue una situación de causa-efecto, pero el caso es que el gol del Espanyo llegó de inmediato. Y lo que era un partido en un solo sentido comenzó a vivirse en las dos áeas. No puede haber debate. Haga lo que haga Mourinho a la hora de encajar a sus piezas, el turco debe estar en el terreno de juego. Ya no es el jugador de destellos, de lagunas, de momentos superlativos y vacíos demasiado largos. No. Ahora Arda es un futbolista para entregarle los mandos del Madrid, para desbordar confianza en lo que tiene y hace. Construir alrededor de su talento será una buena apuesta. Todo lo que no sea eso apunta al error. Fue el primer cambio. Hay cosas que parecen no cambiar. El Madrid ganó, pero sin el turco tuvo mucho menos brillo. En una noche de broncas al Madrid hubo una excepción: Marc Cucurella. El campeón del mundo fue recibido con aplausos desde que se anunció su nombre entre los suplentes blancos. Saltó al campo pasada la hora de partido y se llevó una gran ovación. A un campeón del mundo, a un chico que pasó por la cantera del Espanyol, aunque luego cambiara de acera en Barcelona. Cada disputa entre ellos fue un noble cuerpo a cuerpo para registrar entre las cosas que debe hacer un delantero jugando de espaldas a la meta rival y las que debe ofrecer un central para proteger a su equipo y no verse en desventaja. El ariete del Espanyol, que venía de marcar dos goles en el estreno de Liga, se dio una paliza monumental en un partido poco agradable para un delantero. El central francés mostró argumentos para defender su fichaje y su titularidad. Para el capitán del Madrid fue un partido de brega, de mucho desgaste, de ida y vuelta. Demostró estar en el nivel de ese jugador incansable capaz de cubrir huecos allá donde sus compañeros no llegan. Las opciones para aparecer en ataque no le sobraron. Pero fue un disparo suyo, con el reloj cerca del minuto 80, el que estuvo a punto de tumbar el 1-1. Pero la madera fue su destino final.

Pero fue un disparo suyo, con el reloj cerca del minuto 80, el que estuvo a punto de tumbar el 1-1. Pero la madera fue su destino final.

articles.title: El Real Madrid necesitaba a Carlos Espí
articles.standfirst: Una opinión de José Vicente Hernáez
articles.summary: Una opinión de José Vicente Hernáez
articles.body: Pues claro que sí. El Madrid necesitaba un jugador como Carlos Espí. Tenía a Gonzalo, pero le dieron poca bola. Y desde Joselu no tenía un delantero de esas características. Y cuando lo tenía no lo ponía. Y sin delantero centro es harto complicado ganar partidos. Mbappé no lo es exactamente. Mbappé es un goleador nato. Ante el Espanyol no mojó, pero pudo hacerlo. Parece como si quisiera recuperarlo para la causa, pero de momento eso va para largo. articles.title: Columbia HSFB Team Snaps 101-Game Losing Streak, Longest in History, Led by Former NFL WR as HC
articles.summary: A losing streak that stretched to 101 games is finally over for Columbia High School in Huntsville, Alabama.
articles.body:
A losing streak that stretched to 101 games is finally over for Columbia High School in Huntsville, Alabama.

Columbia beat Greensboro High School 41-14 on Saturday.

"All the glory to God," Columbia coach Sammie Coates said, per AL.com's Thomas Ashworth . "God has blessed me to be in this situation to bring this to this school, to this community. I want to say thank you to the administration, to the school supporting me, having my back the whole time, and the players showing up and fighting every single day throughout the spring, throughout the summer, everything they have done.

"They deserve every moment of this. They stuck it out. Guys came out and helped support. We built the program, and it's coming. We ain't there yet, but we are coming."

Coates, who starred at Auburn as a wide receiver before playing four years in the NFL, is in his second season at the helm. According to Kaleigh Tingelstad and Mike Brown of 48 News in Huntsville, he had just 28 players on the roster by the time the 2025 campaign concluded.

Now, Columbia is 1-0 to kick off 2026, and the Eagles prevailed in emphatic fashion. They reeled off 41 unanswered points after going behind 14-0.

Running back Christian Richey was a standout performer, eclipsing 200 yards from scrimmage and scoring four touchdowns.

Having a coach with an NFL pedigree certainly helped to build Columbia's profile, and the school began working with Gatorade in August 2025 to give its players an added boost.

articles.title: Premier League season predictions: Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville pick the title winner and players to watch in 2026/27
articles.summary: Arsenal tipped to defend their Premier League crown but opinion is split on the race for Europe, relegation and players and managers to watch as Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville make their predictions...
articles.body:
Jamie Carragher and Gary Neville made their 2026/27 Premier League season predictions on Monday Night Football.

Title winners

Jamie Carragher - Arsenal

A few weeks ago, I thought Man City might have a chance - but it was all around Rodri. If Rodri stayed I'd maybe make a case for them, but without Rodri, I just can't see it.

Gary Neville - Arsenal

One hundred per cent Arsenal. They're way out in front. With what they've got already now in defence and in midfield, with the good attackers that they've got, they've got a really good standard, then they're fine.

Top-four finishers

Jamie Carragher - Man City, Chelsea, Liverpool

Man City are better than Chelsea but the European factor can play a huge part. We saw Manchester United last season. It gives them a big lift, Chelsea.

I think Liverpool would want more, but I think just looking at the Chelsea situation, Liverpool where they are right now, I don't see any way they'd be in the top two, and I don't see any way they can mount a title challenge.

Gary Neville - Chelsea, Man City, Man Utd

Chelsea second? Just purely because of the fact that they've got no European football. If they keep Enzo Fernandez, with Moises Caicedo in midfield, with that front three, and they're only playing 45 games, they're going to amass an enormous amount of points.

That's based upon the fact that they're going to have more free weeks, they're not going to have the injury pressures, they're not going to have the travelling that comes with European football, and the mental fatigue that comes with that. I think they'll just edge past Manchester City.

I can't separate Man Utd and Liverpool in fourth place, I genuinely have no idea. I think City are in a better position than United. At the moment, I'm not convinced by United or Liverpool, but I do think they'll finish fourth and fifth.

Fifth and sixth?

Jamie Carragher - Man Utd, Spurs

Gary Neville - Liverpool, Brighton

Sometimes you look at Spurs going, 'oh, they've spent a lot of money' and thinking 'quite exciting for Spurs fans, they're finally splashing the cash'. But then I look at the team and I think, 'where's it all gone?'

Savinho and Omar Marmoush will make them a lot better, but I just don't know whether they'll pull it together and that's the question.

I know Brighton are a good unit, they're reliable, they're consistent and I think Brentford and Brighton, those two teams this season may just get in there because they're consistent and they know what they're doing and they're well-drilled.

A well-organised, well-drilled team will beat a team of talented players who are still trying to find their way.

European contender?

Jamie Carragher - Brentford

A lot of people say, when you're managing a club like Brentford, which is so well-run behind the scenes and the hierarchy, it makes it easier for the manager. Of course it does - but watching them this weekend, watching them last season...

Brentford haven't got European football, so I think that will be a big plus for them. I really love watching Brentford play, and for me, that was the best performance of the week [their win over Spurs].

Gary Neville - Spurs

Relegated

Jamie Carragher - Ipswich, Hull, Sunderland

Why Sunderland? The fact that they've got European football, they're going to be doing a lot of Thursday-Sunday. I think Sunderland last season reminded me a little bit of Sheffield United under Chris Wilder, where they came up and had a really brilliant season, finished high up the table but a lot of the games, like Sunderland, you win by the odd goal.

I'm not saying it's luck but their underlying numbers had them not far away from relegation.

Gary Neville - Coventry, Hull, Ipswich

I hope that one or two of the promoted sides stay up but I've not got the faith I had last season.

Having watched what I've seen this weekend, I'm going to go for the three promoted teams to go down.

Relegation risk

Jamie Carragher - Crystal Palace

Crystal Palace haven't had a great pre-season. They lost the first game at Everton, which, to be fair, they were actually very unlucky when you look at the chances they had. I know they had Europe last season, but a new manager, new in the Premier League, lost a few players, still in Europe... I'd probably go Crystal Palace to have a scare.

Gary Neville - Fulham

Watching Fulham [against Chelsea], that's a risk, that's a big risk. Young players, splitting your centre-backs like that, being open...

Top scorer

Jamie Carragher - Erling Haaland

Gary Neville - Erling Haaland

Impact signing

Jamie Carragher - Mateus Fernandes, Spurs

I really liked Mateus Fernandes last season at West Ham and I thought there might be another few teams in for him, better teams than Spurs.

Gary Neville - Bruno Guimaraes, Arsenal

He's the best signing by a mile.

If you take a player out of Arsenal's team anywhere, probably David Raya is the other one, but in the outfield parts of the pitch, there isn't a drop-off between the first and second choice anywhere, apart from Declan Rice. There's a massive drop when Declan Rice moves out of the team. If Rice gets injured for three months, that would be a risk to Arsenal.

The signing of [Bruno Guimaraes] removes that risk.

He is a massive personality. A different player than Rice but you talk about personality and character on the pitch... he is a brilliant personality. He believes he can win every single football match for his team. He believes he can tackle, he's aggressive, he's somebody you'd want alongside you...And by the way, £75m compared to some of the others that have gone for more is value in this market.

Player to watch

Jamie Carragher - Jeremy Jacquet, Liverpool

He's played one Premier League game and he's only played one pre-season game for Liverpool. [Jeremy Jacquet] looked really good in both games but you know sometimes when you look at a player and they just look the part.

I think this is the first season where a player alongside Virgil van Dijk is going to have to play his own game and at times look after Van Dijk.

Gary Neville - Morgan Rogers, Chelsea

When you're a £120m player you've got to hit numbers. You've got to be 12, 15 goals, you've got to be 10, 12 assists or else you're going to come under pressure.

We know he's a good player, Morgan Rogers. We'd all like him at our clubs. But £120m? Wow.

If he can deliver this season for Chelsea they can go and push Arsenal.

Manager to watch

Jamie Carragher - Matthias Jaissle, Newcastle

He's only young but he's got that little twinkle in his eye. I think Matthias Jaissle will be a fiery character in the Premier League. He's coming to Newcastle, a huge football club, and put in that performance [on Sunday]. I think he's got something about him.

Gary Neville - Xabi Alonso, Chelsea

If he gets the recruitment right and he keeps the players in those front areas of the pitch and he sorts the defence and the goalkeeper out he could be the emerging manager - out of that five that are below Mikel Arteta that are trying to win the league - he could be the next one to win the league

I think this season is critical for him because he's got to finish second or a good third because if he doesn't, without European football, with that squad that he's amassed, then there would be questions.

He's the manager of Chelsea - that means that he basically makes the final decision on transfers, on recruitment. If he goes and does one or two pieces of business in this next week or so, he's got to look after himself and demand that he gets that one or two players in this next week and we know where those areas are.

articles.title: SEC Issues Statement Opposing NFL Players Returning to CFB amid Latest Commits to Lane Kiffin, LSU
articles.summary: With eligibility controversies surrounding LSU and the SEC ahead of the 2026 season, the conference released a statement Monday saying it opposes NFL players returning to the college ranks.
articles.body:
With eligibility controversies surrounding LSU and the SEC ahead of the 2026 season, the conference released a statement Monday saying it opposes NFL players returning to the college ranks.

"College athletes, not former professional athletes, have been at the heart of the Southeastern Conference," the statement said. "Individuals who choose to leave college athletics, sign professional playing contracts, and compete professionally should not then be permitted to return to college competition.

"Allowing that to occur will blur the line between college and professional sports, create significant competitive equity concerns, and reduce opportunities for high school and current college athletes.

"College sports are for college athletes. The current confusion around national eligibility standards emphasizes the need to advance the Protect College Sports Act."

This comes as LSU and head coach Lane Kiffin appear primed to add a handful of players who seemed to be done at the collegiate level.

ESPN's Max Olson noted former Ole Miss tight end Dae'Quan Wright plans to join the Tigers after he clears waivers in the NFL following the Cleveland Browns' decision to waive him. What's more, former Ole Miss defensive lineman Zxavian Harris is also committed to LSU after the New Orleans Saints waived him earlier this month.

Former Notre Dame defensive end Junior Tuihalamaka also committed to LSU.

Olson reported those are three of the 16 players who are now eligible for a fifth year after a Louisiana court granted them a temporary restraining order.

"At the end of the day, because of these rulings, they're either going to play for you or they're going to play for someone else around the country," Kiffin told reporters Monday. "So we've made the decision to recruit them like probably most people are."

It is another step in his aggressive roster-building strategy ahead of what will be his first season at LSU.

He also landed the top-ranked 2026 transfer portal class, per 247Sports , and seems set to add more talent that was competing for NFL roster spots not long ago.

articles.title: Leeds and Rangers co-owner Jed York arrested in Ohio and pleads no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools
articles.summary: Jed York, who owns San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct; York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio; He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences
articles.body:
Leeds United and Rangers co-owner Jed York was arrested over the weekend in Ohio and pleaded no contest to misdemeanour charges of disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools.

Court records show that York, who owns the San Francisco 49ers, was initially charged with engaging in prostitution, but prosecutors amended that to disorderly conduct.

York was charged with possessing criminal tools for using his phone to respond to an undercover online prostitution advertisement, according to prosecutors.

York was arrested Sunday morning at a mobile home community in East Palestine, Ohio, near where he was born and raised in Youngstown. He was released after posting a $5,000 bond.

He was sentenced to one day in jail for both offences to be served concurrently and was credited with one day served when he pleaded no contest Monday morning. He was also fined $1,150.

Records also show that York had his cell phone returned to him and that $160 that was seized was to be given to the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force as part of the plea agreement. York also completed an online course.

Columbiana County Prosecutor Vito Abruzzino said most of these prostitution cases typically end in plea agreements.

"Each case is looked at individually and for specific facts of the conduct, what evidence the police provide, and input from the arresting officer," he said in an email.

"You also have to factor in criminal history of the defendant, and whether or not they have committed these types of offences in the past, and importantly, what the judges will allow."

The 49ers Enterprises - who are the investment arm of York's San Francisco 49ers - own Leeds United. The Premier League club have declined to comment.

They are also part of the US consortium who acquired a majority shareholding in Rangers last summer. However, York is not listed on the club's list of board members.

When contacted by Sky Sports News, Rangers chose not to comment.

A San Francisco 49ers statement read: "As this is a legal matter, which has been resolved, we will not be providing any further comment at this time."

The NFL issued a statement saying the league was aware of the arrest and would review it under the personal conduct policy.

Owners are subject to possible fines or suspensions for violating the personal conduct policy.

articles.title: Carlos Baleba transfer: Manchester United complete signing of Cameroon midfielder from Brighton
articles.summary: Sky Sports News has been reporting on United's interest in Baleba since last autumn and broke the news that they enquired about signing him during the January transfer window; the Cameroon international signs a five-year deal at Old Trafford
articles.body:
Manchester United have completed the signing of midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton.

The Cameroon international, 22, joins the club in a deal worth up to £70m, made up of a £65m guaranteed fee plus £5m in add-ons.

He has signed a five-year contract which includes the option of a further year.

Baleba is currently injured, having picked up an ankle injury in pre-season, but Sky Sports News understands he could be back by mid-September. Manchester United play Manchester City on September 13, live on Sky Sports.

Baleba's arrival at Old Trafford brings an end to a transfer saga that has lasted almost 12 months. Sky Sports News has been reporting on United's interest in Baleba since last autumn and broke the news that they enquired about signing him during the January transfer window.

He remained one of United's top targets this summer and becomes their third addition in midfield after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

"It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams. Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour," Baleba told the club's website.

"I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me reach the highest level.

"The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together."

Baleba joined Brighton from Lille in 2023 and made 112 appearances for the club. He featured 35 times last season and was absent for a spell while representing Cameroon at the Africa Cup of Nations.

'I had no idea what this club would become' - Baleba pens Brighton farewell

Upon the announcement of the news, Baleba took to social media to post an emotional farewell to Brighton.

"I came here at 19 with little English and no idea what this club would become to me," he wrote.

"Brighton only asked me to be myself. The staff who make the club run so well. The team-mates who took the time to understand me, on the pitch and off it. The nights at the Amex when I heard my name from that stand always made me feel at home.

"To all of the fans, staff and my team-mates. You looked after me and for that I will hold you all close to my heart. Wherever I play, this club is in how I play. Good luck Seagulls."

Is Baleba a major gamble or a game-changer for Man Utd?

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

A year ago, Carlos Baleba appeared to have the world at his feet.

A breakout season at Brighton had established the then-21-year-old as one of the Premier League's most coveted young midfielders, with a move to one of Europe's elite clubs seemingly inevitable. Manchester United were among those interested, having identified Baleba as a potential transformative presence in midfield.

But Brighton's reported £100m-plus valuation proved a stumbling block. The move never materialised and Baleba stayed at the Amex.

His form subsequently dipped dramatically. His numbers fell and, at times, he looked a shadow of the midfielder who had generated so much excitement the previous season.

That makes this a gamble for United. But, stylistically, there are few midfielders better suited to what they need.

United require greater authority in the middle of the pitch and, crucially, someone capable of winning the ball back in deeper areas. Baleba brings exactly that. His athleticism, aggression and ability to carry the ball through midfield would add a level of dynamism and steel that is currently missing.

Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have been astute additions, but Baleba offers something different: specialist defensive power coupled with the athleticism to drive United up the pitch.

His age is another major factor. Baleba is still only 22 and, despite his inconsistent season, there remains a belief around him that he can develop into one of the world's best midfielders.

That ambition is reflected in his influences. Baleba has spoken of his admiration for Paul Pogba, Yaya Toure and Andres Iniesta, while Neymar and Ronaldinho were among his favourite players to watch. There is a desire for self-expression in his game that goes beyond the physical qualities that made so highly rated.

There is risk attached to signing him. United would be betting on the player Baleba can become rather than simply the one he has been over the past 12 months.

But if United want to find a midfielder capable of growing into one of the best in his position, this is exactly the sort of gamble they should be willing to take.

articles.title: Liam Delap: Nottingham Forest agree Â£50m deal for Chelsea striker
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest have agreed a fee worth around Â£50m to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap.
articles.body:
Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record fee worth around Â£50m to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

The 23-year-old is expected to undergo a medical and sign a long-term contract at the City Ground this week.

Delap's move comes a year after he joined Chelsea from Ipswich Town for Â£30m amid competition from Manchester United and Everton .

However, Chelsea made him available for sale this summer after he scored just one Premier League goal in a previous campaign disrupted by shoulder and hamstring injuries.

Forest have already signed defender Ousmane Diomande from Sporting for Â£34m, alongside free agents, Austrian midfielder Xaver Schlager and goalkeeper Steve Benda.

They sold England midfielder Elliot Anderson to Manchester City for a club-record Â£116m and striker Taiwo Awoniyi to Coventry City for Â£9m.

Delap's arrival would provide competition for strikers Chris Wood and Igor Jesus, who failed to find the target in Forest's 1-0 defeat by Leeds in their home Premier League opener on Saturday.

Chelsea have also signed two strikers this summer in Emmanuel Emegha from Strasbourg and Danny Welbeck from Brighton .

Delap came up through Derby County's youth system before joining Manchester City in 2019.

After helping City win the FA Youth Cup in the 2019-20 campaign, he scored 24 goals in 20 Premier League 2 matches in 2020-21 as they won the title.

In September 2020 the striker scored on his senior City debut in a 2-1 League Cup win against Bournemouth , and three days later made his Premier League debut in a 5-2 defeat by Leicester.

Injuries played a part in limiting further first-team opportunities, and between 2022 and 2024 Delap spent time on loan in the Championship with Stoke, Preston North End and Hull City .

In the summer of 2024 he was sold for Â£20m by City to Ipswich and scored 12 goals in 37 Premier League games for the newly promoted side.

articles.title: Julian Alvarez transfer latest: Atletico standing firm on Barcelona as Arsenal become only get out for Argentine striker
articles.summary: Julian Alvarez is holding out for a move to Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid are standing firm on the refusal to sell to their LaLiga rivals; Atletico football expert Ruben Uría believes the only way out for Alvarez is to join Premier League champions Arsenal
articles.body:
Julian Alvarez must take one of two paths before the transfer deadline: stay at Atletico Madrid and try to rebuild his connection with the fans or get his head around a potential move to Arsenal.

Atletico have told him again that they will not sell him to Barcelona and that - coupled with the reaction of the club's supporters on Sunday - has left him "devastated", according to well-placed sources in Spain.

The situation is now "extremely tense", according to Atletico expert and journalist Ruben Uría.

"Neither Miguel Gil Marín (CEO of Atlético Madrid) nor the Apollo board want to sell the player to Barcelona," he told Sky Sports News. "The entire Apollo board supports Gil Marín's decision. Alvarez has been told."

According to Uría, Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has remained in contact with his former Atletico employers in recent days after Alvarez was booed off by supporters in the opening LaLiga game against Villarreal.

But Arsenal will need Alvarez to put Barcelona out of his mind and show he really wants to join Mikel Arteta's project before any serious negotiations or any offers can be made. In that vein, Arsenal are not currently hopeful of getting him in before September 1 and they are certainly not currently expecting it at the Emirates.

"We are waiting to see how events unfold regarding Julian, waiting to see how Arsenal reacts, and if they have genuine interest in the Argentina player. Atletico Madrid will not sell to Barcelona.

articles.summary: Football News: Former Man City star Gareth Barry predicts Erling Haaland's eventual departure from the club, discussing the impact of the team's performance on the striker's future. Find out why the next two years are crucial for Haaland and Man City.
articles.body: Erling Haaland's future at Manchester City may be secure for now, but one former City midfielder believes the Norwegian's long-term stay at the Etihad should not be taken for granted.Haaland has committed himself to the club on a contract running until 2034 and remains the centrepiece of City's attack. Yet with the club entering a new era and facing questions over whether it can maintain the dominance of recent seasons, Gareth Barry believes the next couple of years could be decisive in determining whether the prolific striker eventually looks for a new challengeWhy Haaland could eventually look elsewhereHaaland joined City in 2022 and has already established himself as one of the most prolific goalscorers in the club's history.The 26-year-old has scored 162 goals in 200 appearances across all competitions for City, while playing a major role in a period that included a historic Treble in 2022-23. His long-term contract, signed in 2024, was designed to keep one of football's most coveted strikers at the Etihad well into the next decade.But Barry does not believe the length of that agreement necessarily means Haaland will see it through.Speaking exclusively to GOAL, the former England international said: âErling Haaland leaving Man City one day is inevitable.âBarry stressed that Haaland has no reason to force an exit while City remain competitive, and expects the striker to avoid the kind of public agitation that has accompanied some high-profile transfers.âAs much as Haaland's association with City is really big, and that will keep him there for now, he won't be rocking the boat like you see a lot of other players doing,â Barry said.The former City player believes the situation could change if the club's trophy haul begins to decline.âI think if City's dominance does wane a little bit and the trophies aren't coming in, it will fuel the speculation,â he explained. âIt is natural sometimes to want a new challenge, and I'm sure Haaland will be no different.âBarry's prediction is therefore less about Haaland wanting out immediately and more about what happens around him.âIt's not just going to happen overnight. Haaland will think about his career, which is short,â he said. âBut if the trophies aren't coming in, it will just fuel speculation.âAnd given Haaland's standing in the game, Barry expects the striker to have no shortage of options if he eventually decides the time is right.âHe will have offers from all over the world because he's the best striker in the world, so it's just natural. It's one you can see happening in the future.âThe next two years could be crucialFor Barry, the most important period may not be the end of Haaland's current contract but the next two seasons.He believes the striker's eventual decision will be heavily influenced by how competitive City remain domestically and in Europe.âA lot will depend on how competitive City are in Europe and the Premier League in the next year or two, I should imagine,â Barry said.That is particularly significant given the changes taking place around Haaland.Pep Guardiola has departed after his long spell in charge, while City are now entering a new era under Enzo Maresca. At the same time, Rodri has left, removing one of the most influential players from the team's midfield.Those developments have led Barry to question whether City can immediately return to the top of the Premier League.Barry expects Arsenal to be favouritesCity have gone two seasons without winning the Premier League, with Liverpool and then Arsenal restoring themselves to the top of the domestic game.Barry, who helped City win their first Premier League title in 2011-12, believes the latest changes could make a title challenge even more difficult.âEven before selling Rodri, given the turnover of managers at City, it would have been tough to overturn Arsenal from where they are at the moment,â he told GOAL.âI think with Rodri going, they're even less of a threat now to challenge Arsenal.âBarry expects City to strengthen further and believes new additions could ease the burden on Elliot Anderson and the rest of the midfield, but he does not think that will necessarily be enough to make them favourites.âI'm sure they're going to sign one or two to improve and maybe replace him, which will help [Elliot] Anderson and the other players in that midfield,â he said. âI'd say they have less of a chance to challenge and maybe win the title now Rodri is gone. I won't say they've given the title away, but itâs making it a lot harder.âHis assessment of the title race is emphatic.âI have Arsenal down as huge favourites,â Barry said. âI just feel with City, with what's going on, the threat is less and less this season and Rodri leaving has just added to that, really. So I can see the other clubs improving.âHe also expects Chelsea to progress after missing out on Champions League football, while believing Manchester United and Aston Villa could find European competition challenging.Ultimately, Barry still expects City to finish second but sees a sizeable gap between them and Arsenal.âI still think City will possibly be in second place, but they'll be less of a threat than they were last year,â he said.Spain remains a possible destinationHaaland's future has already been linked with the two biggest clubs in Spain.Real Madrid's long-standing pursuit of elite attacking talent means the Norwegian continues to be associated with a potential move to the Santiago BernabÃ©u, while Barcelona are also expected to consider options for the No. 9 position as they plan for life beyond Robert Lewandowski.Those links have existed since Haaland established himself as one of Europe's premier strikers and could become increasingly prominent if City's competitive level drops.A move to Madrid was even part of the platform of former Real Madrid presidential candidate Enrique Riquelme, who promised to sign Haaland had he won the club's election.He did not, leaving the situation unchanged for now.There is no indication that Haaland is currently pushing to leave City, and his enormous contract gives the club significant security. But Barry's argument is that circumstances, rather than the contract itself, could ultimately determine the striker's next move.If City continue challenging for major honours, there may be little reason for Haaland to look elsewhere. If that dominance begins to disappear, however, the equation changes.For a striker who has already achieved extraordinary numbers at the Etihad and who is entering what should be the prime years of his career, the next two seasons could tell City, and Haaland, whether the future is still in Manchester.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Bruno Fernandes: Man Utd captain wins 2025/26 PFA Players' Player of the Year as Bunny Shaw wins women's award
articles.summary: Man Utd's Bruno Fernandes crowned PFA Player of the Year as Man City’s Bunny Shaw wins women’s award for second time; men's Young Player of the Year handed to Man City's Nico O'Reilly as Arsenal's Olivia Smith picks up women's prize; Sir Kenny Dalglish receives merit award
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes has been crowned the men's PFA Players' Player of the Year for the 2025/26 season, as Manchester City's Bunny Shaw won the women's award for a second time.

Playmaker Fernandes broke the all-time record for Premier League assists during an outstanding 2025-26 campaign, setting up 21 goals as he surpassed Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne.

The 31-year-old also scored nine times as United overcame a shaky first half of the campaign to finish third in the Premier League under Michael Carrick and earn a Champions League return.

  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

Fernandes was pleased to have been voted the winner by his fellow professionals.

He said: "It is obviously a very proud moment. They are the ones you go on the pitch against and it's probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment."

The Portugal international is the Red Devils' first winner since Wayne Rooney took home the trophy in 2009/10 and adds to his Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year award from May.

Manchester City sharpshooter Shaw, who was also recognised by the FWA, scooped the PFA Women's Player of the Year award for the second time.

The 29-year-old claimed the trophy in 2023-24 and won it again, having scored 21 goals on the way to a third straight Golden Boot and her maiden Women's Super League title.

O'Reilly and Smith scoop young player awards

Arsenal's Olivia Smith picked up the women's PFA Young Player of the Year title for the second campaign running, having won the 2025 crown for her exploits at Liverpool and continued her form in the capital.

Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly was named men's PFA Young Player of the Year following an outstanding campaign that ended with the versatile talent helping England to win World Cup bronze.

The 21-year-old was part of the PFA Premier League Team of the Year along with City team-mates Erling Haaland, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo.

O'Reilly said: "I had a great season. I'm very proud of the season I had. I won two trophies with my club and managed to play at the World Cup with my country. I'm over the moon how it turned out."

Champions Arsenal had five representatives in David Raya, Gabriel, William Saliba, Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice, with Player of the Year Fernandes of United and Brentford striker Igor Thiago completing the team.

The PFA WSL Team of the Year featured three players from triumphant City, with Shaw joined by team-mates Kerstin Casparij and Yui Hasegawa.

Mariona Caldentey, last year's PFA Women's Player of the Year, was joined in the XI by fellow Arsenal players Emily Fox and Alessia Russo.

Tottenham defender Toko Koga and Manchester United's Jess Park were also included in the team, as were the Chelsea trio of Hannah Hampton, Ellie Carpenter and Lauren James.

EFL awards revealed as Dalglish picks up merit prize

In the EFL, former Middlesbrough midfielder Hayden Hackey, who joined Premier League side Everton this summer in a £24m deal, won the Championship PFA Players' Player of the Year.

Dom Ballard, who joined Bristol City from Leyton Orient earlier this summer, claimed the award in League One, while Swindon striker Aaron Drinan picked up the League Two prize.

Sir Kenny Dalglish and Karen Carney received the PFA merit awards in recognition of their contribution to football.

Dalglish enjoyed a success-laden career as a player with Celtic and Liverpool, and is Scotland's most capped player, having represented his country on 102 occasions.

The 75-year-old, who confirmed in June that he was undergoing treatment for cancer, went on to enjoy a successful managerial career, leading Liverpool to three league titles before masterminding Blackburn's Premier League triumph.

Carney played 144 times for England, including being part of the Lionesses squad which finished third at the 2015 World Cup.

Having come through the ranks at Birmingham, Carney won the quadruple with Arsenal in 2007 as well as a league and FA Cup double with Chelsea in 2018.

articles.title: Jonas Urbig still has fondness for FC Köln, but Bayern Munich was perfect next step
articles.summary: Jonas Urbig cannot say enough about FC Bayern’s club environment.
articles.body:
After spending more than a decade at FC Köln, Jonas Urbig knew that moving to Bayern Munich would be a major change. But according to the young goalkeeper, settling in at his new club happened much faster than he expected.

Speaking to Bayern Munich's club magazine Säbener51, Urbig opened up about leaving Köln and discovering what life is really like inside Bayern Munich:

"I will always have an emotional connection with Köln. I wish the club nothing but the best – unless they are playing against us. At first, I only knew Bayern Munich from the outside. But once I got to know the club from within, I quickly realized how human and open everyone at the club is. From the outside, 'Mia San Mia' can often sound like just a slogan, but today I know that it is genuinely lived here. And that feels really good. That was certainly one of the reasons why I felt very quickly that I was in the right place here," Urbig said (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ).

Urbig's comments offer an interesting perspective on the culture at Bayern Munich. From the outside, "Mia San Mia" can easily be viewed as nothing more than a famous club motto. For Urbig, however, experiencing the environment firsthand has given the phrase an entirely different meaning.

After more than ten years in Köln, leaving a club that played such an important role in his development could never be easy. But Urbig appears to have found a new home in Munich, surrounded by a group that has made him feel welcome from the beginning.

Now, his goal is to continue developing and prove that he belongs at Bayern Munich.

articles.body:
Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad takes place at the Santiago Bernabéu on Wednesday, August 26, 2026, in the rearranged La Liga Matchday 1 fixture. Kick-off is set for 9:00 p.m. CEST, or 8:00 p.m. BST. Real Madrid will play their first home league game of the season after opening the campaign with a 2-1 win away to Espanyol.

Real Sociedad, meanwhile, arrive in Madrid after losing 1-0 to Real Betis . The fixture was moved from its original date because several Real Madrid players were still involved in the 2026 World Cup.

José Mourinho will lead Real Madrid into his first competitive home match since returning to the club. Pellegrino Matarazzo will take charge of Real Sociedad as both teams look to improve their early league position.

Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad will see Mourinho manage a squad affected by early injuries. Éder Militão and Rodrygo are unavailable, while Ferland Mendy , Raúl Asencio and Thiago Pitarch are also sidelined according to the match information supplied. Real Madrid started the season with a 2-1 win at Espanyol, with new signing Carlos Espí scoring the 90th-minute winner. Jude Bellingham had earlier put Madrid ahead before Espanyol equalized.

Real Sociedad began with a 1-0 defeat against Real Betis. Mikel Oyarzabal is among the key players available to Matarazzo, while Álvaro Odriozola remains out with a long-term knee injury. Gonçalo Guedes and Pablo Marín faced fitness checks before the match.

Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad Lineups and Key Numbers

The confirmed Real Madrid lineup includes Thibaut Courtois , Denzel Dumfries , Álvaro Carreras, Federico Valverde , Ibrahima Konaté, Dean Huijsen , Arda Güler, Bernardo Silva , Kylian Mbappé , Jude Bellingham and Vinícius Júnior . Mourinho has selected a 4-2-3-1 formation.

Real Sociedad's starting team includes Álex Remiro , Jon Aramburu , Sergio Gómez , Carlos Soler , Igor Zubeldia , Jon Martín, Takefusa Kubo , Yangel Herrera , Orri Steinn Óskarsson and Luka Sučić, with the final attacking position listed for Gonçalo Guedes in the confirmed lineup. Matarazzo also uses a 4-2-3-1 shape. Oyarzabal is among the substitutes.

Real Madrid have won four of their last five meetings with Real Sociedad. Their most recent meeting at the Bernabéu ended in a 4-1 Real Madrid victory in February 2026, with Vinícius Júnior scoring twice. The teams also played out a 4-4 Copa del Rey draw in April 2025.

Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad: How to Watch and Match Details

Real Madrid vs Real Sociedad kicks off at 9:00 p.m. CEST at the Santiago Bernabéu. Real Madrid's official schedule confirms the match was postponed from Matchday 1 because of World Cup commitments.

In Spain , the match is listed on Orange TV and Movistar LaLiga. Viewers outside Spain can also follow the match through regional broadcasters. Fans in the UK can use Premier Sports or LaLigaTV, while DAZN has coverage in Italy and Germany .

In the US, ESPN+ and ESPN Deportes will carry La Liga, with TSN+ serving viewers in Canada . beIN Sports covers the Middle East and North Africa, while SuperSport provides La Liga coverage across Sub-Saharan Africa.
